title: Signal-led right-sizing & autoscale policy proposals for dedicated fleets
creator: Marco Li
description: Implement a signal-driven pipeline and policy templates to (1) surface per-pool utilization and right-size recommendations, (2) provide conservative throughput guarantees for Dedicated customers, and (3) ship autoscaling policy primitives (damping, cooldowns, burst buckets) that avoid oscillation while meeting customer SLOs. This ticket captures the proposal, tactical implementation plan, acceptance criteria, and next steps for experiments and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A daily and 1-hour rolling utilization signal computed for every dedicated pool (cpu/gpu/ram and token throughput) stored in the metrics table.
2) Right-size recommendation job that outputs pool resizing proposals (scale up/down) with estimated cost delta and risk score.
3) Three autoscale policy templates available in the console: conservative (latency-first), balanced, and aggressive (cost-first), with documented cooldown/damping defaults.
4) Grafana dashboard + alerting for oscillation risk and missed throughput SLOs.
5) Simulation harness that can replay 30 days of traffic and show projected cost and p99 latency for proposal vs baseline.
technical_notes:
- Metrics: use existing ingestion pipeline (prometheus -> long-term TSDB) with a new derived metric 'pool_throughput_tokens_per_sec' and 'pool_utilization_pct'.
- Aggregation: compute 1h, 4h, 24h percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) and peak-rolling-window for burst detection.
- Smoothing: implement EWMA (alpha=0.2) for short-term decisioning; maintain raw percentiles for guarantees.
- Right-sizing heuristic: prefer downsizing only when 7-day p95 utilization < target (target varies by customer tier). Include hysteresis windows to prevent flip-flops.
- Autoscale primitives: implement scale_step, min_capacity, max_capacity, cooldown_seconds, damping_factor. Add 'burst_bucket' to permit short-lived traffic above commit without scaling.
- Simulation: extend existing capacity-simulator with a 'policy' abstraction to test different damping/cooldown combinations.
decisions:
1) Throughput guarantees will be expressed as a 95th percentile sustained throughput over a 1-hour window, with documented tail protection options (customer can opt into 99th).
2) Default right-size targets: P0 customers -> 70% p95 utilization, P1/P2 -> 60% to prioritize latency.
3) Use EWMA smoothing for autoscale triggers to reduce noise; full-window percentiles still used for right-size recommendations.
4) Start with conservative cooldown defaults: 10min cooldown after scale down, 5min after scale up. These will be tuned based on simulation results.
tradeoffs:
- Aggressive downscaling reduces cost but increases risk of missed SLOs during traffic spikes.
- Longer cooldowns reduce oscillation but delay capacity recovery, hurting latency during sudden growth.
- EWMA smoothing masks short spikes (safer for cost) but may delay necessary scale-ups.
- Per-pool recommendations simplify ops but may conflict with tenant preference for headroom; we must surface estimated customer impact clearly.

rollout_plan:
1) Feature flags: 'util-signals' and 'autoscale-policy-templates' in staging.
2) Beta cohort: 10 customers on Dedicated with opt-in autoscale recommendations.
3) Observe for 2 weeks, adjust defaults, then enable 'preview' for all customers.
4) Gate automatic apply behind explicit admin approval and audit logs.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for metric derivation and EWMA.
- Integration test: ingest synthetic traffic and assert scale events follow policy.
- Simulation: run 30-day replays for 10 representative pools.
- Canary: enable recommendations (preview only) for 10 beta customers, monitor p95/p99 and cost delta.
next_steps: 1) Finish console preview UI (DES-214). 2) Wire up export job and email report for pool owners. 3) Run extended simulations and finalize defaults. 4) Create RFC for SLA language updates (legal + sales signoff).
